items.question: What is LearnSlice AI-Mentor?
items.answer: A personal chat-based AI mentor for early-career talent that delivers personalized onboarding, continuous upskilling and on-the-job practice. From day one. That means less repetitive work for your trainers and faster ramp-up for every new hire.

items.question: Is the content exam-aligned?
items.answer: Yes. The platform recreates realistic IHK and university exam scenarios and maps learning paths to regional IHK requirements. No curriculum work on your end. It's built in.

items.question: Can we customise training for our company?
items.answer: Absolutely. Ready-made role simulations are included out of the box, and you can optionally upload internal documents to tailor onboarding, upskilling and lateral-entry (Quereinstieg) scenarios. Most companies are live with custom content within two weeks.

items.question: How does the AI personalise learning?
items.answer: The AI profiles each learner (skills, goals, company needs), creates a bespoke learning plan, and adapts tasks in real time to close knowledge gaps. Trainers see the results in real-time dashboards. No manual tracking needed.

items.question: How is competency proven?
items.answer: Competency is validated continuously with job-relevant checks (quizzes, deep dives and case studies) and realistic simulations - measurable job-readiness, not just completion certificates.

items.question: What engagement mechanics are included?
items.answer: Built-in gamification: points, badges and levels to boost motivation, focus and completion rates. Companies report higher apprentice engagement from week one.

items.question: Will apprentices actually engage with the platform?
items.answer: Most apprentices log in voluntarily multiple times per week once the first two-week rollout settles. The format respects how Azubis learn: short, exam-relevant tasks, gamification (points, badges, levels), and a trainer dashboard that flags any apprentice whose usage drops below the rollout average. Disengagement is caught and corrected early, not at the IHK exam.

items.question: Is my data safe / GDPR compliant?
items.answer: Yes. 100% GDPR-compliant. Data can be stored on German, European or your company systems per your policy. No data leaves the EU unless you choose otherwise.

items.question: How does this help with early contract cancellations and trainer load?
items.answer: Targeted, practice-led learning shortens ramp time, reduces friction and keeps talent engaged, freeing senior staff to focus on strategic work. According to BIBB, an apprentice costs a company about €26,200 a year on average (2022/23). Our savings calculator shows, based on BIBB averages and your own assumptions, what fewer early cancellations and less trainer time can be worth.

items.question: How do we make sure our trainers actually use it?
items.answer: Adoption friction usually comes from trainers being asked to learn a new system on top of their existing workload. LearnSlice is built around that constraint: out-of-the-box simulations and learning paths require zero curriculum work to start, and the trainer dashboard surfaces only the apprentices and items that need attention this week. A 30-minute onboarding plus a single point of contact during the first two weeks covers the typical setup.

items.question: How does pricing & integration work?
items.answer: Billed annually. Core functionality is included; optional customisation or platform integrations may incur additional costs. Free support is provided. Book a demo to see pricing for your team size.

items.question: How fast can we get started?
items.answer: Implementation is designed to be quick: out-of-the-box simulations work immediately, and optional company customisation can be rolled in as needed. Most companies are up and running within days.

research.subheadline: LearnSlice is co-developed in a publicly funded research project with FH Dortmund. Here is what the first university pilot looked at, and what it found.

context.headline: What the study looked at
context.body: LearnSlice was co-developed with the IDiAL institute at FH Dortmund in a research project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE, grant 16GM200302). In May 2026, 50 master's students used it to prepare for an exam in a Usability Engineering course. The evaluation used a Design Science Research approach with two student surveys and a focus group of five lecturers with 8 to 19 years of teaching experience. This is the first of three planned iterations.

challenges.label: The starting point
challenges.headline: Where students said exam prep is hardest
challenges.intro: Before the pilot, students named their biggest exam-preparation challenges. The didactic design responds directly to the top ones. 60% of these students already studied with AI before the pilot, which is exactly why verifiable sources matter.

items.question: Who owns the solution and the data?
items.answer: You do. You own the deployment, the content, and the learner data. It stays in the environment you choose and is never used to train AI models.

items.question: Which privacy and accessibility rules do you build for?
items.answer: Every project comes with a data processing agreement. We build for the GDPR and UK GDPR by default, design interfaces to WCAG AA, and add the oversight and documentation the EU AI Act requires if you have learners in the EU. If your programs fall under FERPA, HIPAA or state privacy laws, tell us in the first call: we host in the US or on your own servers, so the data stays where your contracts say.

items.question: Can you integrate with our LMS and existing systems?
items.answer: Yes. We build new platforms or extend existing ones, including Moodle, Open edX and custom LMS, and connect them through SCORM, xAPI, LTI and single sign-on to the tools your teams already use.

items.question: How long does a project take?
items.answer: A first working version usually takes 6 to 8 weeks. Building on our existing learning engine is much faster: a branded financial-literacy companion went from kickoff to a working MVP in two weeks and was live in production within a month.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: As a market reference: a Chapman Alliance survey of 249 organisations put the average cost per finished hour of custom content at about 10,000 dollars for basic, 18,600 for interactive and 50,400 for advanced, simulation-based e-learning; a full custom platform typically runs from the mid five figures into six figures, and a serious game starts at about 15,000 dollars per module. Four levers drive the price: interactivity, integrations with existing systems, AI and personalisation, and scope and ownership rights. The strategy call turns these ranges into a concrete price range for your project, with no obligation.

link.label: All benchmarks with sources: How much does custom e-learning cost?

items.question: Where is everything hosted?
items.answer: By default in Germany, under the GDPR. UK organisations can use that without extra transfer paperwork, because UK law treats the EEA as adequate. If your data has to stay in the US or the UK, we host it there: on Microsoft Azure in a US or UK region, which we also use for the AI models, or on your own servers.

items.question: We are in the US or the UK. How does working together work?
items.answer: Our team works in Germany and Poland. UK clients share almost the whole working day with us. For the US, we hold calls between 9 AM and noon Eastern, and the work moves forward overnight. Projects run at a fixed price agreed before we start, or as a dedicated team if you prefer.
